pr_title: Feat: Wayland flatpak input support | Remote desktop portal
pr_body:
## Fixes #5949 
## Description:
Utilise the [remote desktop portal](https://flatpak.github.io/xdg-desktop-portal/docs/doc-org.freedesktop.portal.RemoteDesktop.html) interface (provided by xdg desktop portal) when uinput is unavailable for input capture on wayland.
## Advantages:
Wayland input is supported similar to uinput on:
1. Flatpak
2. While dev/debugging (cargo/flutter run)
## Supports:
It supports input from:
- Desktop
- Mobile
- Physical keyboard mobile

Events:
- Key inputs
- Mouse movements, clicks, and scroll (x & y axis)
## Tested:
Remote: ubuntu, arch (kde, gnome)
Local: mac, linux, ios, android
## Note:
During testing, I found an issue that occurs even without the changes of this PR (also occurs on 1.2.3):
- Mobile -> ubuntu wayland flatpak stream freezes but input still works (rdp input; enabled by this PR).
## Build for test/review:
[rustdesk-1.2.4-x86_64_wl_rdp.flatpak](https://github.com/sahilyeole/rustdesk/releases/download/nightly/rustdesk-1.2.4-x86_64_wl_rdp.flatpak)

issue_context.title: Rustdesk can't remote control wayland host (flatpak, Flatpak officially supports input capture through portal)
issue_context.body:
### Bug Description

Rustdesk remote control is not working when the host is running a wayland session. Despite allowing remote control at the connection, the controller side can only see the image of the host machine, but without being allowed to use keyboard or mouse.

The distro I've tested is Manjaro running GNOME, so I don't know if other Distros / Desktop Environments have the same problem. I've tried "Windows -> Manjaro" and "Manjaro -> Manjaro", using rustdesk from source and flatpak, and in all cases I couldn't send mouse and keyboard inputs to the wayland host.

Remote control "Manjaro -> Windows" works as expected.

Specs:
-Rustdesk v1.2.3
-Kernel 6.5.5-1
-Distro: Manjaro x64
-Wayland 1.22.0-1
-Desktop Environment: GNOME 44.5
-Compositor: Mutter 44.5-1
-Flatpak v1:1.15.4-1

### How to Reproduce

-Install rustdesk
-Login in a wayland session
-Allow another client to connect to your session

### Expected Behavior

-The remote connection should be able to control your mouse and keyboard

### Operating system(s) on local side and remote side

Windows 11 -> Linux, Linux -> Linux

### RustDesk Version(s) on local side and remote side

1.2.3 -> 1.2.3

### Screenshots

![rustdesk 123](https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/assets/7890832/1554ebbc-b057-46eb-aa3a-82e29497ad8f)


### Additional Context

[Flatpak officially supports input capture through portal](https://github.com/flatpak/xdg-desktop-portal/releases/tag/1.18.0) so It shouldn't be a problem in this case.

Just an observation that it affects source installation (not just flatpak). Haven't asked about appimage, since appimage itself doesn't support wayland.

>[Flatpak officially supports input capture through portal](https://github.com/flatpak/xdg-desktop-portal/releases/tag/1.18.0) so It shouldn't be a problem in this case.

>Just an observation that it affects source installation (not just flatpak).

The thing is even if flatpak supports input capture from remote we are using `uinput` for emulating input key presses/mouse on wayland and `uinput` requires sudo privilege (in order to access dev/uinput).
On normal installation the rustdesk --service has to be started as root for input emulation.
So to fix this issue we need permission to access to dev/uinput for the flatpak version of rustdesk.
https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/issues/2798#issuecomment-1413028783
You do not have to use uinput, there is flatpak feature. You can write your logic for flatpak.

review_comments: You added this in your PR https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/pull/6628, and now remove it. So why?

In #6628 I skipped supported resolutions on wayland as it doesn't work on wayland and it was making calls to `get_capturables` on loop and hence user prompts on loop.

But in this PR I have changed `get_capturables` so that it makes only one user prompt request no matter how many calls it gets. https://github.com/rustdesk/rustdesk/commit/eff2490081c48c4f251847de5024cb8d0e2a8c1e
So reverting #6628 enables the future possibility of supporting `supported resolutions` on wayland with only one user prompt. Currently, it is working the same with or without it.
